rationale: Tests the absolute contraindication of alkali neutralisation for ingested acid — the exothermic reaction and CO2 generation make it dangerous.
Tests identification of nitric acid's characteristic yellow staining via the xanthoproteic reaction — a forensic identification feature of acid attacks.
Tests the critical contraindication of oil/fat in phosphorus poisoning — phosphorus is highly lipophilic and fat dramatically increases absorption.
Tests the paradox that barium sulphate (used in radiology) is non-toxic while soluble barium salts cause severe poisoning — a classic distinction.
Tests the classic nail finding of chronic arsenic poisoning — Mees' lines are transverse white bands corresponding to episodes of acute arsenic exposure.
Tests the critical contraindication of dimercaprol (BAL) in iron poisoning — BAL forms a toxic complex with iron that is more harmful than iron alone.
Tests the exact Indian BAC threshold under the Motor Vehicles Act — 30 mg/100mL, commonly confused with the UK/US limit of 80 mg/100mL.
Tests the key metabolic distinction — methanol's toxicity is due to formic acid (not formaldehyde), which causes optic nerve demyelination and metabolic acidosis.
Tests the combined atropine + PAM protocol for OP poisoning within the 24–48h window before AChE ageing.
Tests the absolute contraindication of supplemental oxygen in paraquat poisoning — O2 accelerates the free-radical lung injury that paraquat causes via superoxide generation.
Tests the specific antidote for cyanide poisoning — nitrite+thiosulphate combination or hydroxocobalamin, both examinable.
Tests the well-known limitation of standard pulse oximetry in CO poisoning — it reads falsely normal because HbCO absorbs the same wavelength as HbO2.
Tests the critical rule that paracetamol hepatotoxicity is silent at 6 hours — NAC must be started based on the Rumack-Matthew nomogram before liver injury is established.
Tests the contrast between benzodiazepines (charcoal-adsorbed) and lithium (charcoal-NOT-adsorbed) — lithium requires haemodialysis.
Tests the diagnostic triad of opioid toxidrome — miosis, respiratory depression, coma — the key recognition pattern for naloxone administration.
Tests the forensic anchor for insulin homicide — C-peptide is absent in commercial insulin but always present with endogenous insulin secretion.
Tests identification of the Big Four Indian snakes by toxidrome — neurotoxic (cobra/krait) versus haemotoxic (viper) distinction is the core FM13.19 skill.
Tests interpretation of the 20WBCT — a positive result (failure to clot) indicates haemotoxic viper envenomation, NOT normal clotting as often misunderstood.
Tests recognition of the delayed triphasic amatoxin syndrome — the 'honeymoon' asymptomatic phase at 24h is the most dangerous diagnostic trap.
Tests the principle that specimens should be collected before treatment where possible — but never at the cost of delaying life-saving resuscitation.
Tests visual identification of copper sulphate — its bright blue crystalline appearance and green vomitus + haemolysis presentation are classic OSPE features.
